title: The Culture series
subtitle: Iain M. Banks — nine novels and one collection
blurb: Iain M. Banks's Culture books in the order he published them — standalone space opera in a post-scarcity galaxy, plus the short-story collection the source counts with them.
notes: Publication order, and for once it barely matters.

The source lists the series by publication date and so does this page. Each novel is a self-contained story with new characters — the article says so in its first paragraph — so there is no chronology to get wrong. It also says reference is occasionally made to the events of previous novels, which is the only reason an order is worth having at all.
One of the ten is not a novel.

Wikipedia counts the series as nine novels and one short story collection, and The State of the Art is the collection. It is a full row rather than an optional one because the source counts it among the ten, and because two of the works in it are explicitly set in the Culture universe. Like every other row it counts as one.
The source contradicts itself about one year, and this is the one it is.

The State of the Art is dated 1991 by the article's infobox and by the bibliography it cites, and 1989 by the table of books on the same page. This page carries 1991 on the count — two places to one, all three of them the same article. The row's position is not in doubt either way: both of the source's own lists put it fourth.
Inversions is here because the source puts it here.
The article's own entry for it says it is not explicitly a Culture novel, and then files it with the other nine. Tick it or skip it; nothing else on this page leans on it.

Every book counts as one and nothing on this page is weighted. Page counts differ by edition, a page is not an hour, and one weighted row would quietly turn every other row into an hour — so there are none at all.
Titles, years, publication order and the count read from Wikipedia's Culture series article — its infobox, its table of books and its bibliography.

sections.title: The opening run
sections.intro: Publication order is not writing order: the source dates the first draft of Use of Weapons to 1974 and Consider Phlebas's to 1982, eight years later — and Consider Phlebas is the one that came out first. This page follows the shelf, not the desk.

items.note: Short story collection, not a novel · two of its works explicitly set in the Culture universe

sections.title: The middle three
sections.intro: The article's reception section singles out two of these three: Inversions took the 2004 Italia Science Fiction Award for best international novel, and the American edition of Look to Windward made SF Site's best-of-2001 list after the UK edition missed by one place the year before.

items.note: Not explicitly a Culture novel, says the source — which files it here among the ten anyway

sections.title: The last three
sections.intro: The last Culture book he published is the bottom row here, and the eight years in front of Matter are the reason the page splits at all. The article says nothing about what that gap was for, so neither does this.
